sql_schemas: table leave_types | fields: id, name, description, is_active, created_at, updated_at | pk: id | indexes: name: unique lookup by leave type name (annual, sick, emergency, etc.) — used in every leave request creation and balance query; is_active: filtering active leave types for dropdowns and policy resolution

table leave_policies | fields: id, leave_type_id, policy_name, entitlement_days, accrual_rate, max_accumulation, minimum_notice_days, requires_manager_approval, is_active, created_at, updated_at | pk: id | fks: leave_type_id -> leave_types.id | indexes: leave_type_id: policy lookup by leave type when validating entitlements; is_active: filtering active policies for leave request validation; leave_type_id, is_active: combined lookup for the active policy of a given leave type

table leave_requests | fields: id, employee_id, leave_type_id, start_date, end_date, reason, status, approved_by, approved_at, created_at, updated_at | pk: id | fks: employee_id -> employees.id; leave_type_id -> leave_types.id; approved_by -> employees.id | indexes: employee_id: listing leave requests for a specific employee (self-service dashboard); status: filtering by status for manager approval queues and HR reports; employee_id, status: combined lookup — employee filtering their own requests by status; start_date, end_date: date-range queries for calendar views and overlap detection; leave_type_id: aggregating usage by leave type for balance calculations

table leave_balances | fields: id, employee_id, leave_type_id, policy_id, fiscal_year, total_entitlement, used_days, remaining_days, status, created_at, updated_at | pk: id | fks: employee_id -> employees.id; leave_type_id -> leave_types.id; policy_id -> leave_policies.id | indexes: employee_id: fetching all balances for an employee's dashboard; employee_id, leave_type_id, fiscal_year: unique balance lookup per employee/leave-type/year — the hot path for every leave request validation and balance deduction; leave_type_id: aggregating usage across employees for reporting; fiscal_year: scoping balance queries to the current fiscal year
data_notes: Tables defined: leave_types (reference data for annual/sick/emergency/etc.), leave_policies (entitlement rules per leave type), leave_requests (employee leave applications with status lifecycle), leave_balances (per-employee per-leave-type per-fiscal-year tracked entitlement/used/remaining). The leave_balances.remaining_days is a derived field (total_entitlement - used_days) that must be kept consistent on every write. The leave_requests table references employees.id — the employees table is owned by the employee module and is referenced by name only here. Audit records (GP-002) are written to the existing audit_logs table defined in DOMAIN.md; the leave module's service layer calls the audit repository, not a leave-specific audit table.

open_questions.question: How are leave days counted for balance deduction — are start_date and end_date inclusive (i.e. `end_date - start_date + 1`), or exclusive? Are weekends and public holidays excluded from the day count?
open_questions.impact: Every balance deduction across the system — if one query uses inclusive counting and another uses exclusive, balances will drift. This is a BINDING semantic that must be consistent across leave request creation, approval, and balance queries.
candidate_options: Inclusive: days = end_date - start_date + 1 (both start and end count as leave days)
Exclusive: days = end_date - start_date (only full days between)
Business days only: exclude weekends and public holidays (requires a holiday calendar)

transaction_contract: Multi-step writes (approve: update leave_request status + deduct balance + write audit; reject: update leave_request status + write audit; cancel: update leave_request status + optionally restore balance + write audit) must be atomic. Repository methods that must join a caller's transaction accept an optional `client: PoolClient` parameter. When `client` is provided, the method uses it for all queries and does NOT release it. When omitted, the method acquires a client from the shared pool internally and releases it. The calling service owns the unit of work: it acquires a client from the pool, calls `BEGIN`, passes the client to each participating repository method, then calls `COMMIT` on success or `ROLLBACK` on error. Read-only repository methods (findById, findByEmployeeId, etc.) do not require the optional client parameter.
